answer: Split the economy into many small shards, each built on its own shale of scarce admission slots and sealing influence inside its borders, like an orchard divided into walled groves where blight in one cannot reach the next. A willow bends but stays rooted in its grove, and so must an identity: a sybil flood can capture at most the shard it floods, never the whole economy, since cross-shard influence is capped. The limit is shard capture itself: a shard with too few honest members can still be overwhelmed, so each shard needs a minimum honest population.
